rv.q: Without effacing memories of Edward Fox in the role, Atkinson suggests a man whose very niceness is inherently tragic.
Instead it ventures into Chekhov territory, savouring the complexities of the characters’ tangled pasts.

cn.t: Simon Gray's rueful comedy about loneliness stands up well in this respectful revival, with Rowan Atkinson delivering a contained, understated performance in his return to straight theatre after 25 years.
